competitors.rationale: Offers ingredient awareness through fridge photo recognition and recipe suggestions, verified on 2026-08-12 (C:FridgeChef). However, it focuses on individuals improvising single meals rather than household weekly planning or grocery lists.

competitors.pricing_summary: EUR 6.99/month or EUR 49.99/year (converted to approximately EUR 4.17/month)
competitors.rationale: Directly targets families with weekly meal planning, automatic grocery lists, and family sharing, verified on 2026-07-30 (C:MealLoop). It lacks pantry inventory tracking, but dominates the structured planning space.

Offers shared meal planning calendars for couples and flatmates, but data is stale having been last verified on 2024-11-05 (C:PlanPlate). It does not offer inventory tracking or automated waste reduction.
Strong pantry inventory tracking with barcode scanning and expiry alerts, verified on 2026-06-18 (C:PantryGenie). It generates shopping lists but does not build multi-day weekly dinner plans.

competitors.pricing_summary: Free; EUR 29.99 one-off for full recipe pack
competitors.rationale: Focuses on budget meal plans and store price comparisons, last checked 2026-05-02 (C:WeekWise). However, its details are unsourced with no URL provided, and it does not track home inventory.

Provides use-it-up recipes for leftover ingredients, but data is stale from 2025-01-20 and sourced only from a home page (C:ZeroWaste Kitchen). It lacks systematic inventory tracking and weekly scheduling.
Competes directly on shared household coordination, dinner planning, shared lists, and cooking rotas, verified on 2026-08-25 (C:SupperSync). It does not integrate pantry inventory awareness.

white_space: No existing competitor combines dynamic household inventory tracking with automated weekly dinner planning and shopping list generation. Competitors either do inventory/leftovers without weekly plans (C:FridgeChef, C:PantryGenie, C:ZeroWaste Kitchen) or weekly planning without inventory tracking (C:MealLoop, C:PlanPlate, C:SupperSync, C:WeekWise).
pricing_anchors: Monthly list prices across active competitors range from EUR 2.99/month (C:PlanPlate) to EUR 6.99/month (C:MealLoop, which also offers an annual plan of EUR 49.99/year, equivalent to approximately EUR 4.17/month), with mid-tier options at EUR 3.99/month (C:PantryGenie), EUR 4.49/month per household (C:SupperSync), and EUR 4.99/month (C:FridgeChef). S05 indicates a median stated willingness to pay for a cooking app of EUR 3.50/month. Pricing hypotheses must stay within the EUR 2.99 to EUR 6.99 monthly band anchored near S05's EUR 3.50; any higher price point is untested.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Existing recipe apps give ideas but do not know what you already own.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: This claim is contradicted by competitor data showing existing apps that recognize or track owned items: C:FridgeChef provides recipes from fridge photos, C:PantryGenie tracks pantry inventory with barcode scanning, and C:ZeroWaste Kitchen suggests recipes for leftover ingredients. The true differentiation lies in uniting inventory tracking with weekly planning, not inventory awareness alone.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Dinner planning is a daily chore, groceries are expensive, and a lot of food gets thrown away.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: S01 proves households discard 19% of purchased food, S02 establishes two-person weekly grocery spend at EUR 118, and S04 shows adults spend 22 minutes daily deciding what to cook (noting S04 is from 2023).
